ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system, the vertices of rectangle $OABC$ are such that vertex $O$ is at the origin, side $OC$ is on the positive half-axis of the $x$-axis, and side $OA$ is on the positive half-axis of the $y$-axis, with $OA=3$, $AB=4$. The graph of the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{k}{x}$ (where $k>0$) intersects the sides $AB$ and $BC$ of the rectangle at points $D$ and $E$, respectively, and it is given that $BD=2AD$. For a point $P$ on the segment $OC$, does there exist a point $P$ such that $\angle APE=90^\circ$? If such a point exists, find the coordinates of point $P$; if it does not exist, please explain why.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Exist. Assume there exists the required point $P$ with coordinates $(m,0)$,\\
$\therefore OP=m$, $CP=4-m$.\\
$\because \angle APE=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle APO+\angle EPC=90^\circ$,\\
Also $\because \angle APO+\angle OAP=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle EPC=\angle OAP$,\\
Also $\because \angle AOP=\angle PCE=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \triangle AOP\sim \triangle PCE$,\\
$\therefore \frac{OA}{CP}=\frac{OP}{CE}$,\\
$\because OA\cdot CE=OP\cdot CP$.\\
$\therefore m(4-m)=3$,\\
Solving: $m=1$ or $m=3$.\\
$\therefore$ There exists the required point $P$, with coordinates $\boxed{(1, 0)}$ or $\boxed{(3, 0)}$.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system, the vertices of rectangle $OABC$ are such that vertex $O$ is at the origin, side $OC$ is on the positive half-axis of the $x$-axis, and side $OA$ is on the positive half-axis of the $y$-axis, with $OA=3$, $AB=4$. The graph of the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{k}{x}$ (where $k>0$) intersects the sides $AB$ and $BC$ of the rectangle at points $D$ and $E$, respectively, and it is given that $BD=2AD$. For a point $P$ on the segment $OC$, does there exist a point $P$ such that $\angle APE=90^\circ$? If such a point exists, find the coordinates of point $P$; if it does not exist, please explain why.
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Exist. Assume there exists the required point $P$ with coordinates $(m,0)$,\\
$\therefore OP=m$, $CP=4-m$.\\
$\because \angle APE=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle APO+\angle EPC=90^\circ$,\\
Also $\because \angle APO+\angle OAP=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle EPC=\angle OAP$,\\
Also $\because \angle AOP=\angle PCE=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \triangle AOP\sim \triangle PCE$,\\
$\therefore \frac{OA}{CP}=\frac{OP}{CE}$,\\
$\because OA\cdot CE=OP\cdot CP$.\\
$\therefore m(4-m)=3$,\\
Solving: $m=1$ or $m=3$.\\
$\therefore$ There exists the required point $P$, with coordinates $\boxed{(1, 0)}$ or $\boxed{(3, 0)}$
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is rectangle OABC in a rectangular coordinate system, O is at the origin, OA goes upward along the positive direction of the y-axis, OC goes rightward along the positive direction of the x-axis, A is at the upper left, B is at the upper right, and C is at the lower right. The inverse proportional function curve passes through point D on the upper side AB of the rectangle and point E on the right side BC, and point P is located on the bottom side OC. Reasoning: From OA=3 and AB=4, it can be obtained that A=(0,3), B=(4,3), and C=(4,0). Because BD=2AD and AB=4, AD+BD=3AD=4, so AD=4/3, therefore D=(4/3,3). Point D is on y=k/x, so k=(4/3)·3=4, and the function is y=4/x. Point E is on BC, that is, x=4, so E=(4,1). Let P=(m,0), where 0≤m≤4. To make ∠APE=90°, vectors PA and PE are perpendicular. PA=A-P=(-m,3), PE=E-P=(4-m,1). The dot product is PA·PE=(-m)(4-m)+3·1=-m(4-m)+3. Set the dot product to 0, obtaining m(4-m)=3, that is, m^2-4m+3=0, solving gives m=1 or m=3. Both are within the interval [0,4], so such a point P exists.

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is rectangle OABC in a rectangular coordinate system, O is at the origin, OA goes upward along the positive direction of the y-axis, OC goes rightward along the positive direction of the x-axis, A is at the upper left, B is at the upper right, and C is at the lower right. The inverse proportional function curve passes through point D on the upper side AB of the rectangle and point E on the right side BC, and point P is located on the bottom side OC. Reasoning: From OA=3 and AB=4, it can be obtained that A=(0,3), B=(4,3), and C=(4,0). Because BD=2AD and AB=4, AD+BD=3AD=4, so AD=4/3, therefore D=(4/3,3). Point D is on y=k/x, so k=(4/3)·3=4, and the function is y=4/x. Point E is on BC, that is, x=4, so E=(4,1). Let P=(m,0), where 0≤m≤4. To make ∠APE=90°, vectors PA and PE are perpendicular. PA=A-P=(-m,3), PE=E-P=(4-m,1). The dot product is PA·PE=(-m)(4-m)+3·1=-m(4-m)+3. Set the dot product to 0, obtaining m(4-m)=3, that is, m^2-4m+3=0, solving gives m=1 or m=3. Both are within the interval [0,4], so such a point P exists.
